title: Transport resilience presets, idle-probe policies, and streaming backpressure examples for Cross-SDK
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: SDK consumers across Python, TypeScript, and Go are repeatedly asking for concrete out-of-the-box transport profiles that balance connection reuse, latency, and reliability for both request/response and streaming workloads. Current guidance is scattered and often language-specific.

Goal: Deliver a small set of documented, cross-SDK transport presets (e.g., interactive-low-latency, batch-high-throughput, streaming-resilient) and example snippets showing idle-probe/keepalive settings, per-route connection pool sizes, and streaming backpressure/reconnect patterns. Presets should be safe for Redwood hosted API customers and provide clear upgrade/migration guidance for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope: Produce presets, implement examples in Python/TS/Go SDK docs, add runtime telemetry hooks for connection lifecycle events, and ship a single cross-language reference page in the public SDK docs. Not in scope: changes to server-side connection scheduling or new server APIs (those will be separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Three named presets added to SDK docs: interactive-low-latency, batch-throughput, streaming-resilient
Example code for Python, TypeScript, and Go demonstrating: setting idle probes/keepalive, configuring per-route connection pool size, and safe streaming reconnect/backoff patterns
Telemetry events emitted for conn_open/conn_close/stream_reconnect across SDKs (spec + examples) and backing dashboards linked
Presets include recommended defaults (pool size heuristics), rationale, and trade-offs documented
Docs reviewed and approved by SDK leads (PM + Eng) and reachability tested with Redwood hosted API
migration_notes: Users on older SDK versions: keep existing defaults until they opt-in to presets. We'll provide a migration guide describing the behavioral changes (e.g., shorter connect_timeout, more aggressive pool reuse) and a compatibility table. For Dedicated/private customers, recommend testing presets in staging with load tests and providing an override to pin pool size to existing observed concurrency. Include guidance for Kubernetes liveness/readiness interplay for services that use persistent streaming connections.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for config parsing across each SDK
- Integration tests against a staging Redwood API deploying controlled latency and connection churn (simulate idle timeouts, server resets)
- End-to-end test for streaming reconnect: start a long-running stream, kill connection at server, verify SDK reconnect policy fires and app receives reconnect callback for non-idempotent streams
- Telemetry validation: ensure conn_open/conn_close counts match simulated connections and appear on dashboard
- Backwards-compat smoke: ensure apps that do not set presets behave exactly as before

Test matrices: python-sync, python-async, ts-node, ts-browser, go-native. CI will run regressed tests under two concurrency profiles: low-latency (10rps, 512B responses) and high-throughput (500rps, 8KB responses).
